area: After a successful task-scoped commit, the index is restored to a snapshot taken before HEAD moved, leaving the just-committed files staged for deletion while the attempt reports no residue
finding: The task-scoped commit transaction parks foreign staged entries, commits, then restores the index from a snapshot captured before the operation began. Restoration is correct for entries that existed in that snapshot, but it is applied against a HEAD that the commit itself has advanced. A file that was untracked before the commit has no entry in the snapshot, so restoring it means removing its index entry — and once that file is in the new HEAD, an absent index entry is no longer 'untracked', it is a staged deletion of content that was just committed. The parking mechanism protects foreign work exactly as designed; the fault is that the restore target was never rebased onto the new HEAD. What makes this expensive rather than merely wrong is the reporting: the attempt record reports committed with an empty residue rollback list, so the operation asserts a clean postcondition while the index disagrees with HEAD on every path it just wrote. An operator who trusts the receipt and commits again will delete the files they just added.
expectedBehavior: A restore that runs after HEAD has moved must reconcile against the post-operation HEAD, not replay a pre-operation snapshot verbatim. Paths the operation itself committed should end at parity with the new HEAD; paths it parked should return exactly as they were. The general rule is that a snapshot is only a valid restore target while the baseline it was taken against still holds — once the operation changes that baseline, restoration must be expressed relative to the new one. Independently, the postcondition must be verified rather than assumed: an attempt may only report an empty residue set after comparing the index against HEAD for the paths it touched, so that a divergence surfaces as a receipt instead of as a silent trap for the next commit.
evidenceOrRepro: 2026-08-16, ATM-GOV-0369, governed commit c30eb0820dbd560cf6959066b5e19a4619a84434 via `git commit --auto-stage`. The commit itself was correct: 11 files, exactly the resolved bundle, no foreign content. Immediately afterwards `git status --porcelain` reported the three newly added backlog item shards simultaneously as D (staged deletion) and ?? (untracked) — consistent with `git ls-files -s` returning no entry for them while `git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>` confirmed the content was in HEAD and the worktree copies were byte-identical to it. Three of the task's own task-event files landed in the same state, and the backlog projection showed MM. `git commit-status --json` reported status committed, phase committed, headAdvancedDuringAttempt true, errorCode null, and liveIndexResidueRollback []. The pre-existing staged deletion belonging to another task was preserved untouched throughout, before and after, confirming the parking half of the transaction works. Repair required re-adding the seven affected paths; the index then matched HEAD with the foreign staged deletion still the only remaining one.
followUp: Cover the case directly: a successful commit that adds a previously untracked file must leave that path at parity with HEAD, asserted by comparing index to HEAD rather than by observing that the commit succeeded. Note that the existing ATM-GOV-0369 acceptance for blob-by-blob restoration is written for admission and pre-commit failure paths; this instance is the success path, where the same snapshot is replayed against a baseline the operation moved, so a fix scoped only to failure handling would leave it standing. Distinct from [ATM-BUG-2026-08-12-001], where reconciliation genuinely fails on index.lock contention and correctly leaves a durable receipt — here reconciliation reports success and leaves nothing to find.
